VitalEats Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitalEats Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitalEats Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, gross margin analysis drivers and trends, EPS guidance and key assumptions, revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, performance in key channels retail foodservice convenience, and discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies.

First, regarding impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: We've navigated significant challenges from rising input costs and supply chain issues this quarter, but our proactive measures have helped us outperform peers in maintaining gross margin resilience. In the broader macro environment, USDA and Bloomberg data show double-digit inflation in key food and beverage inputs. Corn, vital for our snacks and cereals, jumped 18% year-over-year to about $7.50 per bushel due to U.S. Midwest droughts and Chinese export demand. Wheat rose 22% from Ukraine tensions, hitting our bakery and pasta lines. Dairy like butterfat and cheese increased 15%, worsened by avian flu cutting U.S. milk output by over 1.5 billion pounds year-to-date. Sugar and cocoa climbed 12% and 25%, with cocoa at multi-decade highs from West African El Niño deficits. Packaging, including aluminum cans and corrugated shipping, rose 10-14% amid energy volatility.

Supply chain woes added pressure: Port congestion in Los Angeles and Long Beach extended ocean freight by 10-15 days, Red Sea reroutes hiked spot rates 40% month-over-month, and North American truck rates surged 25% from driver shortages per DAT Trendlines, leading to $45 million in extra freight costs—about 150 basis points to COGS. In APAC, typhoons delayed Indonesian palm oil for our noodles and spreads, raising landed costs 8-10%. EMEA saw EU fertilizer curbs post-Ukraine inflating vegetable oils 20%, and LATAM currency drops in Brazil and Argentina boosted import costs for fruit beverages.

For Q3, input inflation drove 17% higher commodity costs, or $320 million headwind, plus $75 million from supply chain, totaling $395 million—12.5% of COGS—and 280 basis points gross margin compression to 35.4% from 38.2%. That's better than peers like Kellogg's 390 bps or Mondelez's 320 bps drop. Snacks and Confectionery took the biggest hit at 350 bps due to cocoa and nuts, while Beverages held at 180 bps with less perishability.

We've countered over 65% through layered strategies. Pricing averaged 9.2% increases, recovering $285 million with elasticity at -2.1 and volume down just 1.8% versus category 3.2%. In North America, 55% of revenue, premium pricing on brands like VitalHarvest organics offset private label deflation. Hedging covered 70% of 2024 exposure—corn at $6.20/bushel, wheat at $7.80—below spot, with multi-year deals via ADM and Cargill securing 40% of 2025 wheat 10% under futures. Dairy partnerships buffered 60%.

For supply chain, we diversified palm oil 25% to Malaysia and sunflower from Ukraine to Argentina. AI demand forecasting via SAP IBP cut disruptions 15%, holding service at 97% despite 5% SKU stockouts. New micro-fulfillment in Texas and Ontario trimmed last-mile 12% and airfreight from 8% to 3%. Innovation like 10% sugar cuts in beverages with stevia saved 5%, akin to PepsiCo's Gatorade Zero, while pruning 12% low-margin SKUs boosted mix 120 bps. Alt-protein R&D hedges bird flu risks.

North America took 60% of the impact but volumes grew 1.2% ex-pricing on staples demand. EMEA held via 11% pricing against 8% UK inflation. APAC had 20% inflation but 15% pricing in India's packaged foods. LATAM gained from peso but faced avocado shortages.

Forward, inflation eases to 8-10% in Q4 with USDA corn at $5.80/bushel and freight down 15-20% per Drewry. Margins expand 100-150 bps to 36.5-37% with 7-8% more pricing and 75% hedging. EBITDA holds at $1.65-1.70 billion for FY24, up 5%.

Second, concerning EBITDA margin performance and key factors: Our adjusted EBITDA margin hit 19.5% for the year to date, up 70 basis points from last year and the third straight year of gains. Q3 reached 20.1%, 110 bps above prior year, from pricing, mix, and efficiencies.

Revenue grew 4.2% organically, pricing added 5.8 points, strong in Snacks where 7-9% hikes on NutriCrunch bars and chocolate nuts offset 45% cocoa to $10,000/ton. Hedging 85% of 2024 at $4,200/ton limited passthrough to 1.2 points.

Gross margins up 140 bps to 38.2%, with 220 bps from volume/mix. Plant-based like OatFlex milks and BeyondBeef patties grew 22%, now 15% of sales. Supply chain productivity added 90 bps, cutting waste 12% via AI in 25 North American plants.

SG&A fell to 12.1% of sales, down 90 bps, via SAP S/4HANA saving $45 million in procurement while holding marketing at 8.5%. E-commerce hit 18% NA revenue with 15% ROI on Instacart/Amazon.

North America at 22.3% margins, up 120 bps on snacking and Sparkle sodas gaining 2 points share. EMEA 17.8% resilient vs. 25% energy hikes. APAC 18.9% up 150 bps on RTD teas. LatAm 16.5% despite FX.

Our Margin First framework invests $250 million capex in sustainable packaging and precision ag. FY24 guide 20.0-20.5%, assuming mid-single inflation and 3-4% growth.

Third, in terms of impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: With over 60% of our $4.5 billion Q3 revenue international—from ZestEnergy drinks, NutriCrunch snacks, AquaPure—we faced FX headwinds, but hedging and resilience kept us strong. Reported growth 2.1%, organic 6.4%, FX drag 4.3 points or $650 million, versus 1.2% tailwind last year on USD strength.

Europe 28% revenue, euro down to 1.08 vs 1.12 shaved 2.8% or $120 million, but organic 7.2% on OatBliss plant snacks. APAC 22%, yen -8% YTD minor 1.5% drag, organic 9.1% on RTD teas. Emerging ex-China 18%, 12.4% hit from Brazil real -15% and Turkey lira -25%, $330 million lost, but organic 8.7%. NA 32% neutral, 5.2% organic on premium snacks.

Hedged 85% 2024 via forwards/collars at 1.10 EUR/USD, saving $80 million. 75% local COGS hedges naturally; $200 million capex localizes like Mexico aseptic. Pricing 4-6% in high-FX spots held share.

Q4 FX eases to 2-3%; dynamic pricing and Vietnam sourcing build resilience. Organic 6.4% sets up 5-7% full year.

Fourth, looking at gross margin analysis drivers and trends: We hit 38.7% gross margin, up 150 bps YoY from 37.2%, 40 bps sequential, TTM 38.1%—highest in five years, above 37-39% target. Two-year stack +320 bps from pandemic lows.

Waterfall: Pricing +220 bps from 8-10% hikes—9% on CrunchVita snacks, 11% PureFlow vs PepsiCo/Gatorade. Mix +110 bps, PlantPeak dairy +28% now 14% revenue, 500-700 bps richer. Efficiencies +80 bps, VitalFlow saved $45 million—15% ocean freight nearshoring, AI yields to 98.5%.

Headwinds: Commodities -110 bps (cocoa +22%, wheat +14%), mitigated 60% hedging cocoa at $2,800/MT vs $3,600 spot. Logistics/FX -30 bps.

Trends upward: Q4 FY23 inflection, 40-50 bps quarterly. Deflation ahead 5-8% wheat/corn, sustainability ag 30% wheat at 10% less cost. Digital blockchain cuts waste 1.5%, pea yields +12%.

NA 40.2% +180 bps, EMEA 36.5% +90 bps, APAC/LATAM 35.8% +120 bps. FY24 target 39.5%, +140 bps from pricing/mix/savings. Divesting low-margin dairy, focusing high-ROIC innovation.

Fifth, reviewing EPS guidance and key assumptions: FY24 EPS $2.72-$2.82, 13% growth midpoint over $2.42, above Street $2.78. Assumes stable macro.

Sales 5-7% reported, 4-6% organic: 2-3% volume from HealthForward 42% sales, Zero-Sugar Spark/NutriBars +12% share. Pricing 2-3%. NA mid-single e-comm 18%; EMEA low-single; APAC/LATAM high-single.

Margins +120-150 bps to 38.5-39% via SupplyChain 2.0—AI inventory -15%, waste -8%. Inputs -5% dairy/oils, cocoa $8-9k hedged 80%. SG&A 22.5% -50 bps, $60M savings.

Bridge: Organic +$0.25, margins +$0.18, productivity +$0.10, FX -$0.03, shares 245M post-buybacks. Capex 3.5% sales.

Premium strategy, $1.2B M&A powder. Risks inflation/China; upside premium.

Sixth, analyzing revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Incorporating Q3, we're revising upwards: organic sales 7-9% from 6-8%, pricing 5.5% YTD, volumes 1.5-2.5%. EPS $4.85-$5.05 from $4.70-$4.95, +$0.12 buybacks ($450M YTD). EBITDA margins +190-220 bps to 20.0-20.3%. FCF $1.4-1.6B, capex $900M.

Snacking +4% volumes Circana; CrunchVita +22% share. Beverages Zest Hydrate +35%. NA +10%, EMEA mid-single OatEssence +12%, APAC/LATAM surprises Brazil +8% China +25%.

SupplyChain 2.0 AI forecast error -25%, hedges 90% cocoa $4,200 vs $7,800. Divestiture $180M, 92% top-2 positions. Risks CPI>3.5%; loyalty app 88% retention.

Seventh, examining performance in key channels retail foodservice convenience: Channels drove 82% of $2.8B Q3 revenue, +6% reported +8% organic amid 4.5% food-away inflation.

Retail 48% $1.34B +9% organic vs +4% category: +7% price/mix, better-for-you 35% +15%; ACV +2pts 78%, club/e-com +12/+25%. U.S. +10% back-to-school, Europe +6%, LATAM +14%. Velocity Engine AI +15% facings.

Foodservice 28% $784M +2% organic vs traffic -3%: QSR +4% Yum! $50M, institutional +8% plant patties. Pricing +5%. NA +3%, APAC +7%. Foodservice 2.0 RFID +10% accuracy.

Convenience 24% $672M +15% vs +7%: energy shots +30% 7-Eleven, share +1.5pts. Basket +9%, U.S. +16% Wawa. Conquest 5,000 doors.

Outlook low-teens convenience, mid-single others; margins +200 bps to 38.2%.

Eighth, considering discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: RGM delivered 8.2% organic: 5.1% pricing, 2.3% mix/volume, 0.8% trade. Vs sector 4-5%.

Pricing 4.8% YoY 85% portfolio: Beverages 6.2% sugar/alum elasticity -1.8; Snacks 5.5% cocoa right-sizing -1.2; Dairy 3.9% value eng. NA 6.1%, EMEA 3.7%, APAC/LATAM 5.4%.

AI engine 75% SKUs, PROS/SAP 92% accuracy, +$150M revenue. Trade 22% -120bps. Premium 28% sales +1.2%.

FY24 4-6% pricing, innovation pods. Outpace IRI 2-3%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $4.5 billion, representing a 6.5% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by input inflation partially offset by pricing and efficiencies. Operating income was $675 million, and earnings per share were $0.92. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 6-8% and adjusted EPS of $4.90-$5.10.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, John. As I detailed earlier, input inflation and supply chain added about $395 million headwind this quarter, but our 9.2% pricing, hedging at favorable strikes, and diversification mitigated 65%, limiting compression better than peers. We're set for margin expansion in Q4 as costs moderate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Johnson (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Mia Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our HealthForward innovations like PlantPeak expansions and Zest Hydrate functionals are ramping, targeting 15-20% of incremental sales from premium better-for-you items. Expect them to drive 2-3 points of mix benefit and support mid-single volume in key channels like convenience and e-comm next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Kim (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We've diversified sources—25% palm oil shift, AI forecasting cutting disruptions 15%, and micro-fulfillment reducing last-mile costs 12%. Service levels at 97%, positioning us ahead as freight normalizes 15-20%.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Lisa, our revised FY24 guidance reflects strong Q3 momentum—organic 7-9%, EPS $4.85-5.05, margins 20.0-20.3%. Balanced across regions and channels, with efficiencies and hedging offsetting risks like cocoa. Confident in delivery.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in VitalEats Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
